cases.rationale: The passage states that the treatment group showed a 12% reduction in hospital admissions, directly confirming the claim.

One passage supports the claim by stating a 12% reduction in hospital admissions overall. However, it specifies that this reduction was not statistically significant in participants over 70, which complicates the blanket assertion across all age groups.
The passage P1 states that marathon finishing times did not improve with supplementation and that the supplement group was on average slower than the placebo group, contradicting the claim.

The passages discuss meditation and hypertension but do not provide specific evidence regarding daily meditation lowering systolic blood pressure by at least 8 mmHg in hypertensive adults. Therefore, there is insufficient information to verify the claim.

The passages engage with topics related to temperature and pressure but do not provide specific information confirming or contradicting the claim about water boiling at approximately 100 degrees Celsius at sea-level atmospheric pressure.
The passage P1 states that vaccine efficacy against symptomatic infection was 66%, which contradicts the claim of 95% efficacy.
The evidence passage P1 states that participants were followed for a median of eight years and dietary intake was recorded annually, matching the claim exactly.

The passage states that the medication lowered LDL cholesterol by 30%, supporting that part of the claim. However, it contradicts the assertion that cardiovascular risk was eliminated, as it mentions that 'residual risk remained substantial in all treatment groups.'
The claim states that screen time among teenagers declined, while passage P1 states the opposite: 'Average daily screen time among teenagers rose each year from 2015 to 2020.'

The passages discuss the retraining programme's structure and regional unemployment but do not provide specific information about the employment rate of participants or any changes related to it after one year.

The passages do not address the specific claim regarding the number of chambers in the human heart. They are related to heart function and cardiology but do not provide information about heart anatomy.

The passages discuss the trial's outcomes related to systolic blood pressure and body weight, but they do not mention sleep quality at all. There is no evidence to support or contradict the claim regarding sleep quality.

The passages discuss the 2019 survey and its respondents but do not specifically mention trust in television news. There is no evidence directly supporting or contradicting the claim about trust in television news.
Passage P1 states that moderate drinking can potentially lead to elevated blood pressure, which supports the claim that moderate alcohol consumption may increase blood pressure.
Passage P1 states that 58% of patients reported at least one side effect, which falls within the range of 30% to 60%.
The claim states that participants received 500 g of vitamin C daily, while the evidence specifies that they received 500 mg daily, which directly contradicts the claim regarding the quantity.
The passages establish that the emissions policy took effect in January 2019, which directly contradicts the claim that it took effect in 2015.
Passage P1 states that 'Alphaxin showed no significant reduction' in migraine frequency, directly opposing the claim that it reduced frequency by 40%.

Passage P1 establishes a consistent association between night-shift work and metabolic syndrome, supporting the claim. However, it also states that causality has not been established, which leaves uncertainty about whether night-shift work actually causes metabolic syndrome.

The passage supports the claim that the program increased vaccination coverage by 15 percentage points but contradicts the part about nationwide adoption, stating that 'a national rollout was proposed but has not been adopted.'

One passage states a 12% improvement in endurance performance due to the supplement, while another passage reports no improvement in endurance performance with the supplement. This presents a direct contradiction regarding the claim's central assertion.
